newsitem.title: MEXICO: Third Mexico city opens long-distance phone market.
newsitem.headline: Third Mexico city opens long-distance phone market.

text.p: The long-distance telephone market opened up to competition in Puebla on Monday, the third Mexican city this year to see an end to Telefonos de Mexico's decades-old monopoly.

The first 63,758 lines, out of a total of 200,491 in the city, were opened to rival operators on Monday, and the Communications Ministry calendar provides for the rest to be opened on Tuesday and Wednesday
Queretaro, in central Mexico, and Monterrey in the north, were the first two cities to be opened to competition.
A total of 60 cities, which account for about 80 percent of the long distance market, are scheduled to be opened to competition by July this year.
